newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan seeks eight German vessels, eyes weapons.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan seeks eight German vessels, eyes weapons.

text.p: Pakistan has agreed to buy three ships from Germany and is interested in buying another eight, German deputy defence minister Bernd Wilz said on Tuesday.

He told a news conference that Islamabad had also shown an interest in German weapons, but said his country was at present ready only for more defence cooperation in training, education and medical fields.

"Germany has agreed for (the sale of) three offshore vessels and you (Pakistan) have asked for eight more," he said after two days of talks with Pakistani officials, including Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and military generals.
He did not specify the type of vessels but said they could be used by coastguard against drug trafficking and other crime.

Asked if Islamabad had shown interest in buying German arms, Wilz said the Pakistani defence ministry secretary Iftikhar Ali Khan and generals had "told me of their interest, that's absolutely correct".
He said at the moment Germany could "do more and more" only in the fields of training, education and medicine.
Wilz said Germany was providing training and education facilities for Pakistani military officers and also wanted to send some its own officers to Pakistani military institutions.
